The result was 6% below our expectation ( but was in line with the Bloomberg consensus), due to lower gains on NPL settlement and NPA sales than we had assumed. 1Q26 net profit comprises 13% of our full - year forecast of Bt1.7bn. Result highlights The positive highlight of the 1Q26 financial statements was lighter LLPs than we had assumed. The negative highlight s were lower gains on NPL settlement and NPA sales than we had expected. BAM’s cash collection was Bt3.0bn for the quarter, down by 5% YoY and 25% QoQ. Gains on NPL settlement during 1Q26 totaled Bt 361m (47% below our assumption), down by 41% YoY and 26% QoQ. Gains on NPA sales for the quarter came to Bt 296m (41% below our estimate), down by 25% YoY and 61% QoQ. BAM’s credit cost for the quarter was 3.70% (below our assumption of 4.60%), down from 5.91% in 1Q25 and 6.17% in 4Q25. The AMC spent Bt 130m to acquire distressed debt stock during 1Q26, down 90% QoQ (BAM didn’t buy distressed debtstock in 1Q25). BAM’s net debtstock (cost) totaled Bt66.6bn at end-Mar 2026, down by 12% YoY and 3% QoQ. Net NPA value (cost) was Bt 41.0bn at end-Mar, up by 8% YoY and 1% QoQ. Outlook Our model points to 2Q26 net earnings dropping YoY (no big-ticket NPL settlements or NPA sale s) but rising QoQ (seasonally greater gains on NPL settlement and NPA sales). What’s changed? We forecast a 2026 bottom-line of Bt1.7bn, down 5% YoY, led south by lower gains on NPA sales. Recommendation BAM’s secured NPL settlement and NPA sales operations look set to remain soft this year, as our BLS house economist forecasts GDP growth of just 1.4% YoY, so b anks will maintain tight credit -screening for new loan applications and many clients are likely to delay decisions to settle NPLs and acquire NPAs. Our SELL call stands.
